glossary.m: the big lesson a story teaches, said as a full sentence
a person who checks writing and fixes capitals, punctuation and spelling
the name of one particular person, place or thing, like Lucy or Cair Paravel. It starts with a capital.
a part of a word with one vowel sound. Garden has two: gar and den.
the main part of a word that holds its meaning, like port, which means carry
a comparison that uses like or as
telling the truth, even when it is hard

cards.title: World Notes: Lions Made of Stone and Metal
cards.sub: A real thing behind the story
cards.todo: Read the note. Then read with your lens in mind.
text: People have carved statues of lions for thousands of years, from stone like marble and granite.
The four giant lions in Trafalgar Square, London, look like stone, but they are made of bronze, a metal. They were put there in 1867.
In Chapter 16, the Witch has turned a real lion to stone. Aslan breathes on him, and gold color creeps along his back until he is alive again.

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it's Opti. You finished the book! Today you look back from the first chapter to the last.
transcripts.guide1: Word work: match root words, find four kinds of mistakes, and find syllable types.
transcripts.guide2: Look back through the book. Then watch my video in Read Like a Writer.

notes.wordParts: Roots from this year: inter = between, trans = across, form = shape, ject = throw, script and scribe = write, port = carry, struct = build.
notes.grammar: An editor checks in passes. Capitals for names and the first word. Apostrophes for belonging and joined words. A comma before and or but when it joins two complete thoughts.
notes.spelling: Syllable types: closed (cat), open (go), silent-e (bake), vowel team (rain), r-controlled (car), consonant-le (table).
notes.wgrd: A theme needs proof from across the book. Edmund betrays his family, he is forgiven, and in the end he is crowned King Edmund the Just.
vocab: the supreme ruler of a country or kingdom
the ceremony in which a ruler is officially crowned
restored to friendship or peace after a conflict

mods.script: [warmly] Here's today's reading tip. Look back from the first chapter to the last. What changed? That change points to the theme. Then tap one of the two lenses below to use while you read. You don't need to write anything.

mods.todo: Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or B and type it the right way.
mods.script: Let's fix a sentence. The correct one first. The battle was over in a few minutes, and Peter and Aslan shook hands. The starts with a capital. A comma comes before and, because it joins two complete thoughts. Peter and Aslan are names. Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or Sentence B, and type it the right way.

mods.script: [curious] Here's a poem by Sara Teasdale. Read it out loud. Find the fire that sways and sings. What kind of figurative language is that? Answer out loud.

mods.todo: Tap a word, then tap what it means. Match all four words.
mods.script: Watch one match first. Transfer. Find the root: trans. It means across. To transfer is to move something across to a new place. That's my match! Read the Remember box. Then tap a word, and tap what it means. Match all four words.

mods.todo: Tap a word, then tap its meaning. Match all four words.
mods.script: Ever met someone truly amazing? Remarkable. The book says the Professor was a very remarkable man. Remarkable means so unusual it's worth talking about. Now tap a word, then tap its meaning. Match all four.

mods.todo: Think about the four questions. Tap Check yourself. Then tap every word that is wrong.
mods.script: Four rules, one sentence. the fauns scarf was red and lucy liked it. The needs a capital to start the sentence. Faun's needs an apostrophe: the scarf belongs to the faun. A comma goes before and. And Lucy is a name. Tap Check yourself. Then tap every word that is wrong.

mods.todo: Read the rule. Tap every silent-e, vowel-team or r-controlled word.
mods.script: Pattern hunt! The goat ran to the lake. Goat: two vowels, one sound, a vowel team. Tap! Ran: short a, closed. No tap. Lake: silent e. Tap! Read the rule. Then tap every word in the two sentences with a silent-e, vowel-team or r-controlled syllable.

mods.todo: Look back through the whole book. Then try the Truth Watch below.
mods.script: No new chapters today. Look back through the whole book, from Lucy's first trip through the wardrobe to the crowning. Then try the Truth Watch, and watch my video in the Read Like a Writer box.

mods.label: Opti shows you how
mods.script: Let's try all three parts with a sentence from Chapter 16. Instead of all that deadly white the courtyard was now a blaze of colors. Part one, read like a reader. The statues are alive, and the courtyard is bright. Part two, read like a writer. Two pictures: deadly white, then a blaze of colors. Instead of flips one into the other. Part three, mimic. Here's mine: Instead of all that gray snow, the yard was now a carpet of green grass. Now it's your turn with the museum and the zoo. Write one sentence in each box.

mods.todo: Answer each question in full sentences. Use details from the book.
mods.script: Three questions, in full sentences. One, three moments from different chapters that prove the same theme. Two, Edmund at the beginning and at the end. Three, the one moment that proves your theme best.

mods.todo: Edit your response for capitals, apostrophes and commas.
mods.script: Today you edit. Check your capitals, your apostrophes and your commas, like an editor. Then read your response out loud once, and write the fixed version.

virtue.title: Truth Watch: Is someone being honest?

items.t: In Chapter 5, Edmund says he was only pretending, and that he never went into Narnia.
items.why: He had been there. He lied to make Lucy look silly.

items.t: Lucy keeps saying Narnia is real, even when the others laugh at her.
items.why: She tells the truth even when no one believes her.

items.t: At the end, the children tell the Professor the whole story about the missing coats.
items.why: They explain what really happened, even though it sounds hard to believe.
